messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Severity: S2 — Multiple GPU OOMs observed in the decode/streaming pool (us-west1). Impact: request drops and partial stream responses. Error pattern: CUDA OOM in decoder loop. Triggering alerting and paging @mike-oncall.

mike-oncall: ack, I'm on it. seeing the spike start ~10:23 UTC. node gpu-wn-12 is flapping (OOM then crash then restart). preliminary numbers: ~120 dropped requests/min at peak, 5xx rate up to 6% for streaming endpoints. collecting logs now.

alex-sre: digging into logs — repeated failures in cudaMalloc and then decode loop abort. also noticing a cluster of requests with unusually large `max_tokens` headers, some as high as 20000. looks like a client-side header mismatch + no server-enforced cap. suspect runaway generation causing memory blowouts.

alex-sre: sample log snippet:
```
E/Decoder 10:24:11.342 gpu-wn-12 decode.cpp:472 cudaMalloc([]) failed: out of memory
E/Decoder 10:24:11.342 request_id=abc123 user=customer-42 max_tokens=20000 seq=stream
stack: decode_loop at decode.cpp:472
```

jess-platform: immediate mitigations we can do now: 1) enforce a global per-route max_tokens cap (1024) at the router, 2) enable aggressive KV cache eviction for decode pool, 3) route traffic for heavy/misbehaving API keys to a smaller quantized fallback model. I'll prepare the router override.

priya-eng-runtime: I can push a middleware hotfix to reject client `max_tokens` > 2048 with a 4xx instead of letting it reach the runtime. canary that to 5% before broader rollout. patch snippet below:
```
# runtime/middleware/max_tokens_guard.py
if request.headers.get('max_tokens', 0) > 2048:
    return 400, {"error":"max_tokens exceeds allowed limit"}
```

mike-oncall: applying router cap now (per-route override). will throttle at 1024 and enable prefix eviction.

mike-oncall: running commands:
```
# set per-route override
curl -X POST https://internal-console/api/routes/override \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","max_tokens":1024}'

# scale decode pool while we stabilize
kubectl scale deploy/decode-pool -n serving-us-west1 --replicas=6
# recycle the flapping pod
kubectl delete pod gpu-wn-12 -n serving-us-west1
```

deploy-bot: hotpatch deploy started: runtime-middleware v2.1.3 -> canary (5%). Scaling decode-pool replica count to 6.

deploy-bot: scale command accepted, pods scheduling.

mike-oncall: after the override and scale, OOM events dropped ~90% in the next 3 minutes. still seeing occasional OOMs during long streaming sessions, likely tail cases where max_tokens still high or KV cache pressure remains.

alex-sre: set up an automated fallback routing rule to route sessions with large token budgets or high token-rate clients to `gpt-open-30b-q8` (quantized). rule applied. command used:
```
routectl set-fallback --match "header:x-client-token-rate>1000" --target gpt-open-30b-q8
```

jess-platform: CS update — initial customer impact triage: 11 customers reported 5xx/partial streams in the last 15m. one enterprise (AcmeCorp) had ~120 failed requests during the spike. recommending a status page update and outreach.

cs-team: drafting message to affected customers now (short update + ETA). flagging AcmeCorp as P1 for targeted follow-up.

priya-eng-runtime: recommending a follow-up change to the runtime: 1) enforce soft per-request memory budget, 2) pre-validate `max_tokens` header at edge, 3) instrument per-key token-rate metrics for automated throttles. I'll open the MR and link for postmortem.

mike-oncall: monitoring metrics — request drop rate back to baseline within 10 minutes. latency for streaming endpoints normalized after routing to fallback. flags: need to verify no data corruption for partial streams.

alex-sre: note — the root cause appears to be an upstream client that started sending an incorrect `max_tokens` header due to a regression in their SDK that defaulted to a high value. runtime didn't enforce caps and the decoder accepted the budget, leading to aggressive allocation and eventual CUDA OOM.

jess-platform: incident severity -> downgraded to S3 (impact contained, mitigations in place). post-incident actions: assign postmortem owner, gather timeline, collect offending requests and sample prompts, add regression alert for sudden `max_tokens` spikes, and add a permanent router-side hard cap of 4096.

incident-bot: Severity changed: S2 -> S3. Postmortem owner assigned: jess-platform.

mike-oncall: handing over to day-shift SRE (alex-sre) in 2 hours. I'll prepare timeline and notes. thanks all for quick triage. :thumbsup:

priya-eng-runtime: created MR: runtime/guard-max-tokens — will run CI and land after canary verification. linking in postmortem.

deploy-bot: hotpatch canary successful, rollout to 100% scheduled (+10m) if no regressions.

cs-team: status update posted to customers; AcmeCorp notified and a follow-up scheduled for their support window.

jess-platform: next steps — document timeline, root cause write-up, and permanent mitigations (router hard cap, runtime guards, token-rate throttles). I'll own the follow-up and schedule a lessons-learned session.

incident-bot: thread closed for active paging. monitoring continues for 1 hour. if OOMs reoccur, reopen.

mike-oncall: closing out from night shift, will add any final logs to the incident thread before handoff.
